points: Avis's contract ends in September 2026, so a major revenue stream disappears in Q3 and Q4; the replacement tolling framework is expected to be materially less favorable, so margins are likely to compress even if some revenue is recaptured.
Government Solutions momentum is probably too small to fully offset the Avis loss and keep total revenue from declining in the next print and beyond.
If the next print shows costs rising or cash flow falling, the platform-margin bull case will weaken.
The NYC camera contract bump of $12 million and the 34% five-year DOT increase are already reflected in recent results, so they are unlikely to deliver a fresh upside surprise.
Verra was forced out of Ontario after the November 2025 camera ban; if similar bans spread to other states or provinces over the next 12-18 months, the enforcement-camera growth story would shrink.
Peer CNXC reports on October 1, and if it flags pricing pressure or margin erosion in outsourced services, it would add sector confirmation to the VRRM short right after VRRM's print.

The recurring-revenue, platform-based bull case depends on sticky high-margin contracts; losing Avis and accepting a less favorable replacement deal undermines that narrative and could reset how the stock is valued.
